overlays.title: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act — Covered Residential Eviction
overlays.rule: For a covered premises occupied as a primary residence by a servicemember or the servicemember's dependents, and within the statutory rent-cap framework, eviction during military service generally requires a court order. If military service materially affects ability to pay and an application is made, the court must stay proceedings for 90 days unless justice and equity require a longer or shorter period, or adjust the lease obligation.
overlays.warning: SCRA coverage depends on current covered military-service status and statutory conditions. Veteran status alone does not create this protection.

overlays.title: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act — Default Judgment Protections
overlays.rule: Before entering certain default judgments, courts require information about whether the defendant is in military service, and the statute provides attorney/stay protections in specified circumstances.
overlays.warning: This is not a substitute for appearing in court when possible.

overlays.title: Fair Housing Act — Disability Reasonable Accommodation
overlays.rule: Disability discrimination can include refusing a reasonable accommodation in rules, policies, practices, or services when the accommodation may be necessary to afford an equal opportunity to use and enjoy a dwelling.
overlays.warning: An accommodation request is not an automatic defense to eviction. Coverage, necessity, reasonableness, causation, timing, and statutory exceptions can matter.

overlays.title: HUD-VASH
overlays.rule: HUD-VASH combines HUD Housing Choice Voucher rental assistance with VA case management and supportive services for eligible Veterans experiencing homelessness.
overlays.warning: Voucher availability, local administration, eligibility, and placement are not guaranteed.

overlays.title: Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF)
overlays.rule: SSVF grantees provide homelessness-prevention and rapid-rehousing assistance to eligible very-low-income Veteran families through local providers.
overlays.warning: Services, funding, eligibility determinations, and local availability vary.

overlays.title: Legal Services for Veterans — Homeless Veterans and Veterans At-Risk for Homelessness (LSV-H)
overlays.rule: VA funds legal services for eligible Veterans who are homeless or at risk for homelessness through grantees whose services can include housing-related matters and other civil legal needs.
overlays.warning: Not every grantee provides every listed legal service.
